fixer.summary:
T-30 is fixed. An owned item's value now comes from one place on the Item, so a per-item `cost` prop sets its sale price.

What changed:
- **`dungdra/items.py`**: I added `Item.listed_cost()`. It returns the `cost` prop if the item has one, otherwise the equipment-table price, or None if the item has no price. `unit_cost()` now just calls it and still returns 0 for an unpriced item, so the material-cost check in spells.py behaves as before.
- **`sale_price()`** now takes an Item instead of a name and works from `listed_cost()`. It is still half the value rounded down, and it still refuses an unpriced item.
- **`dungdra/gear.py`**: `sell()` passes the item itself to `sale_price`. Before, it passed `it.base`, which skipped the `cost` prop. The `sell_value` override still works.

I left `buy()` and `craft_plan()` on `item_cost(name)`. Both price a catalog name before any Item exists, and the table price is the same source `listed_cost()` falls back to. Building a temporary Item there would use up an item id and change nothing.

The ticket lists no acceptance tests. The existing selling test (EQP-04: a longsword sells for 750 CP) still passes. New unit tests cover the cost-prop override, unpriced items, rounding down, the refusal, and selling through `gear.sell`. No SRD tags were added because this refactor adds no rule.

Checks run: the new unit tests (8 passed), the full `pytest -q` (594 passed), `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (clean), and `python -m scripts.srdloop dev-gate` (PASS).

followups.title: sell() keeps a second value override beside `cost`: the `sell_value` prop replaces sale_price(it) after it is computed (gear.py:168). Fold it into the item valuation, e.g. a `sale_price` hook on Item that honours `sell_value` and otherwise halves listed_cost(), so selling has one value mechanism. Also the sale_price docstring says trade goods keep full value, but the function always halves.

review.summary:
I'm approving this change. Selling now prices the item you actually own: `sale_price` takes an `Item` and uses the new `Item.listed_cost()`, which applies the `cost` prop when the item has one and otherwise falls back to the equipment table. `unit_cost()` is now built on `listed_cost()`, so there is only one place that works out an item's value.

The diff doesn't touch `buy` (gear.py:147) or `craft_plan` (gear.py:251). That's correct: both take a catalog name, not an item someone owns, so no `cost` prop exists yet and the table price is the right one. The ticket's "~251" most likely meant the old `sale_price(name)` in items.py, and that is what changed.

The new unit tests check real behaviour:
- **Selling:** the money the purse gains, the item leaving the inventory, and the `sell_value` override still working.
- **Valuation:** the `cost` prop override, rounding down when halving, and refusing to price an item with no listed cost.

Nothing is out of scope. I filed one follow-up: the `sell_value` prop is still a second override in `sell()` on top of `cost`. Also, the `sale_price` docstring says trade goods keep their full value, but the function always halves the price.
